capabilities: Push a note's markdown to a file in a local project folder
Push or pull to a custom path via terminal-style folder navigation
Pull a project file's content into the current note
Validate the configured local project folder path
disambiguation: Not a version control system like Git; push and pull commands overwrite files and no history is tracked.
extras: The external requirement is a local filesystem path to a project folder, not a remote service. Files are paired by filename between Obsidian and the project, so renaming in one place requires renaming in the other; hyphenated filenames are recommended. The author solicits donations via buy-me-a-coffee.
problem: Publishing Obsidian notes to a local blog or static site project requires manually creating files and copy-pasting content, and keeping the two copies in sync is tedious.

relations.evidence: Works with Astro.js, Next.js, and any other framework configured to render markdown pages.
Works with Astro.js, Next.js, and any other framework configured to render markdown pages.

requires.name: a local blog, portfolio, or static site project folder

summary: Pushes Markdown notes to a local blog or static site project folder and pulls project files back into Obsidian notes.
